title: Google introduces 'Preferred Sources' button to help publishers combat AI-driven traffic losses
summary: Google has launched a new interactive 'Preferred Sources' button for publishers to embed on their websites, allowing readers to mark them as trusted sources. This feature aims to mitigate traffic losses caused by AI-powered search and content discovery tools. When selected, preferred sources are highlighted more frequently in Google Search, Discover, and Google News. Google reports that users are twice as likely to click through to preferred sources. Additionally, Google is introducing AI-powered customization for Discover feeds and audio briefings in the Google News app.
key_points: Google introduces a 'Preferred Sources' button for publishers to embed on their websites, allowing readers to mark them as trusted sources.
Preferred sources are highlighted more often in Google Search, Discover, and Google News, potentially driving more traffic to publishers.
Google reports users are twice as likely to click through to preferred sources when available.
The feature is part of Google's effort to address traffic losses caused by AI-powered search and content discovery tools.
Over 345,000 unique sources have already been selected as preferred since the feature's launch in May.
Google is also introducing AI-powered customization for Discover feeds, allowing users to refine their content preferences using natural language commands.
Android users will soon be able to customize audio daily briefings in the Google News app.
